title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
passages: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born on 27 January 1756 in Salzburg, a city tucked among the mountains of what is now Austria. Salzburg was ruled by a prince ARCHBISHOP, and its churches and palaces rang with music. Mozart was a true PRODIGY. By about age 5 he was writing small pieces, and his father Leopold took him and his sister Nannerl on long tours across Europe. They rode in bumpy coaches to cities such as Munich, Paris and London, where crowds marveled at a little boy playing the HARPSICHORD with great skill.

In 1781, when he was 25, Mozart moved to Vienna, the busy capital of a huge empire, where people loved concerts and the theater. There he wrote some of his most famous operas. The Marriage of Figaro opened in 1786, and Don Giovanni followed in 1787 in Prague, a city whose audiences adored him. In 1791 came The Magic Flute, a playful tale full of magic and a bird catcher named Papageno. Mozart died in Vienna on 5 December 1791, at just 35. In his short life he wrote more than 600 works, including about 22 operas and dozens of symphonies for a full ORCHESTRA.
